provenance.method: Question assembled from reviewed games whose first-party descriptions explicitly remove goals, fail states, win/lose states, timers or punishment. It does not use user genre tags as evidence.

question: Which games can I inspect if I do not want mistakes to cost me much?
why_it_matters: Failure states, lost progress, punishment and score pressure can make experimentation or returning after a mistake disproportionately stressful.
current_understanding: Tiny Glade and Gourdlets explicitly describe no failure states; SUMMERHOUSE says you cannot win or lose; Townscaper has no goal; The Shape of Things states no punishment system and no timers. These are unusually strong low-consequence mechanics, but none proves that a player will experience the game as emotionally low-stakes.
evidence_needed: More governed records for loss of progress, undo, reset, hint and failure consequences across current games.
reopening_conditions: Any listed game introduces or changes progression, failure, score or punishment mechanics.
A structured game-facet contract becomes machine-readable in the object model.
dissent: Self-imposed perfectionism or puzzle difficulty can create high personal stakes even when the software itself does not punish mistakes.
